messages.text: looping in here — I pulled their account history and the add-on we're working on is $85K net new. but the base renewal underneath it is $310K. so if we lose them entirely trying to push the add-on at the wrong time, that's a much bigger number at risk. think we need to be careful about how we're sequencing this

that's exactly the right framing Erin. what's your read — do we pause the add-on conversation and focus on retention first, or do we think the add-on actually helps the case for staying? I don't want Vince walking into a commercial conversation if the relationship isn't in a good place

honestly I'd pump the brakes on the add-on for now. if they're already skeptical on the product roadmap the last thing we want is to make it feel like we're selling them more when they haven't gotten full value out of what they have. I'd prioritize a strong EBR, get someone senior in the room, and make sure the ERP integration concern is addressed directly — either with a commitment or a workaround

agreed. and I think Vince needs some air cover here — he's been managing this solo and it sounds like things have quietly drifted. not throwing him under the bus but he could probably use a hand getting back in front of the right people over there

ok let's get Vince on a call this week — me, Erin, Vince. want to hear directly from him what the relationship actually looks like and figure out if we need to escalate or if we can stabilize this internally first before bringing in Amy
